# Linearized Yang-Mills Spectral Gap on the Poincaré Homology Sphere

13 Pages Posted: 5 May 2026

See all articles by Blake Shatto

## Blake Shatto

Independent Researcher

Date Written: April 18, 2026

### Abstract

We compute the spectral gap of the gauge-covariant Hodge Laplacian for linearized SU(2) Yang-Mills theory on the Poincaré homology sphere M = S 3 /2I, where 2I is the binary icosahedral group of order 120. The positive Ricci curvature of S 3 provides a universal lower bound on the gauge-covariant Hodge Laplacian via the Weitzenböck identity: all physical (coexact) gauge fluctuations around any flat connection satisfy λ ≥ 2/R 2. 
The flat-connection moduli space is finite, consisting of exactly three isolated points (trivial, standard inclusion, and Galois conjugate), each with vanishing first cohomology H 1 (M ; ad ρ) = 0. Explicit spectral computation via the McKay correspondence for the extended E 8 diagram yields the coexact 1-form spectral gap at each vacuum: ∆ 2 = 4/R 2 for the trivial and standard vacua, and ∆ 2 = 36/R 2 for the Galois conjugate vacuum. The icosahedral symmetry filters the first four coexact levels from the Galois sector, producing a ninefold enhancement over the baseline gap. 
The existence of a positive gap follows from discreteness of the spectrum and vanishing cohomology at all flat connections, which are topological; the quantitative floor 2/R 2 and the explicit eigenvalues are specific to the round metric.

Keywords: Poincaré homology sphere, spectral gap, Yang-Mills, McKay correspondence, gauge theory, Weitzenböck identity

## “Regularisation by noise and notions of irregularity”

Venerdì 26 Giugno 2020, ore 11:00 - Zoom - Lucio Galeati (University of Bonn)

Abstract

A natural question in the field of regularisation by noise phenomena is to understand under which conditions on a path $w$, the additively perturbed ODE $x’=b(x)+w’$ is well-posed, even when its unperturbed counterpart $x’=b(x)$ is not. In order to answer this question, Catellier and Gubinelli (SPA 2016) introduced the theory of nonlinear Young integrals and the concept of $\rho$-irregularity of $w$; they also proved that fBm paths are $\rho$-irregular. In this talk, I will first review their work and then present its more recent extensions.

The property of $\rho$-irregularity can be linked to the regularity of the local time of $w$ and, in the case of Gaussian processes, can be established under a suitable local non-determinism (LND) condition. Moreover, it can be shown that $\rho$-irregular paths are necessarily nowhere $\alpha$-Holder continuous, for suitable values $\alpha=\alpha(\rho)$. This gives a rigorous proof of the frequently observed paradigm “the rougher the noise, the better the regularisation”.

Based on joint works with Massiliano Gubinelli.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Abstract

Let M be a compact simply connected Riemannian manifold which contains a non-trivial closed geodesic γ such that the curvature is constant and strictly negative in a neighbourhood of γ. We show that in this case a Poincaré inequality for the H^{1} gradient on the free loop space C(S^{1},M) endowed with Bismut measure does not hold. Similar results hold w.r.t. more general metrics, and also on based loop spaces with base point close to γ. A key ingredient in the proofs is a result which shows that in a certain sense, the concentration of a Brownian bridge on hyperbolic space near the geodesic joining the end points x and y increases rapidly as d(x,y)→∞.

## Abstract

The infinite Brownian loop {B t 0​,t≥0} on a Riemannian manifold M is the limit in distribution of the Brownian bridge of length T around a fixed origin 0, when T→+∞. It has no spectral gap. When M has nonnegative Ricci curvature, B 0 is the Brownian motion itself. When M=G/K is a noncompact symmetric space, B 0 is the relativized Φ 0​-process of the Brownian motion, where Φ 0​ denotes the basic spherical function of Harish-Chandra, i.e. the K-invariant ground state of the Laplacian. ## Abstract

Let $Q$ be a round spherical space form of odd dimension $n\ge5$, and let $M$ be a closed connected Riemannian manifold. Suppose their scalar spectra admit a partial matching with a fixed error in frequency. For quotients of even order and scalar lens spaces of odd order at least five, an explicit bound on the unmatched count, of order $R^{(n+1)/2}$ at frequency $R$, forces a round universal cover for $M$; for homogeneous $Q$ it forces isometry. The exponent is sharp. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
